item.title: 'You're not welcome here' - Chelsea's Fofana booed by own fans
item.description: Wesley Fofana has made 10 appearances for Chelsea this season. [Getty Images] Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana was subjected to repeated boos and told "you're not welcome here" by his own fans during Friday's Premier League defeat by Nottingham Forest. The jeers aimed at the 25-year-old were heard every time he touched the ball and came after an unauthorised interview with French YouTuber Zach Nani was released. In that controversial two-hour conversation, Fofana also appeared to joke about missing his penalty during last month's Carabao Cup shootout defeat by Liverpool. Manager Xabi Alonso said the French centre-back had apologised and "it won't be repeated". But Fofana endured a difficult time in his side's trip to Forest as supporters made their feelings known. After Chelsea went behind to a brilliant volley from Igor Jesus in the fifth minute, Fofana also conceded a penalty for the home side's second goal from Morgan Gibbs-White in the 51st minute. He was booked for the foul on Liam Delap in the box, and then replaced by Levi Colwill in the 56th minute - just after Emmanuel Emegha had pulled a goal back for the visitors - before Gibbs-White made it 3-1 in the 72nd minute. Emegha scored again in the 89th minute to make it 3-2, but Forest held on to secure their first win over Chelsea at the City Ground since 1997. Meanwhile, Nani has moved to defend Fofana, saying the player was "clearly" not happy during the interview and admitted he had to perform better. Fofana also explained he opted to take a penalty against Liverpool as one of the senior players on the pitch, having joined in a £75m move from Leicester City in 2022. But he confessed football had reached a stage where he was "more unhappy than happy", before recovering physically and mentally. The release of the interview has coincided with the club's poor run of form, with Chelsea losing 4-1 at home to Leeds United last weekend to make it three defeats in four matches. The defence, in particular, has come in for criticism, with the Blues one of four clubs to have conceded more than 20 goals in the Premier League after 11 matches. Having been subjected to racist abuse in the past, Fofana spoke about handling comments during a club-organised interview on this summer's pre-season tour of Asia. He is understood to be one of the highest earners at Stamford Bridge. Fofana has apologised for interview - Alonso Interviewer defends Fofana after backlash

item.title: DK Metcalf’s sign language celebration explained as he sends Aaron Rodgers message
item.description: Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images DK Metcalf responded in style following a difficult past week for him with a touchdown in the opening quarter against the Denver Broncos. The Pittsburgh Steelers had to return their attention to the on-field action after what has been an incredible past few days for the franchise. Wide receiver Metcalf headed into the game on Friday without his usual quarterback, Aaron Rodgers. Metcalf had only scored two touchdowns this year prior to the game against Denver, with his first-quarter score seeing him pull out an impressive sign language celebration. What DK Metcalf’s sign language celebration actually meant This is not the first time Metcalf has used this celebration in the NFL. The wideout has previously pulled a similar celebration out during his stint with the Seattle Seahawks. However, there will be very few fans who will have known the exact meaning behind it. Reporter Arye Pulli claimed Metcalf said, “Stand on business, 8″. Rodgers, of course, was number eight for the Steelers, with Metcalf seemingly showing his support for the former quarterback. Despite struggling to show it on the field, Rodgers and Metcalf had formed a strong connection since they both landed in Pittsburgh. It is a telling statement of where Metcalf’s loyalties lie when it comes to the ongoing saga between Mike McCarthy and Rodgers. As for Metcalf, it is about time he showed his worth on the field, with the receiver making three catches from his four targets inside the first half. Having narrowly avoided a suspension following his actions last week against the Philadelphia Eagles, Metcalf has said a lot without even opening his mouth when it comes to the feud between his head coach and now-former quarterback. item.title: Neemias Queta on importance of center play for Boston Celtics, NBA
item.description: According to Boston Celtics head coach Joe Mazzulla, the center position is the most important on any team in the NBA right now, and Boston big man Neemias Queta is inclined to agree. "I'm a center, so I'm a little bit biased, but the amount of responsibility that you have, the most efficient shots are at the rim," said ( via CLNS Media) the Portuguese center when asked about Mazzulla making such a claim in a recent Boston press conference. Noting how much pla on both ends of the court goes through big men in the NBA of today, Queta highlighted "being able to create as many easy looks at the rim offensively, whether it's through screening" as being critical. "Whether it's me getting the the dump downs, whether it's being able to being able to be a offensive rebounding guy and make make those shots, and then defensively deterring people from getting out there." "I think that impacts a lot of the game because everything else is tough shots, and we can we can play easier defense," added the Boston big man, who sees his success at center last season as more of a baseline than something to replicate. "This year is a new new season," he explained. "Whatever I did last year doesn't even matter anymore, so I'm just trying to build off of this season and keeping on growing off of the previous game." "But if I can have this year be like last year's ceiling, be my this year's floor, I think I'm in a good spot. And I think that's that's where I'm trying to get to and (continue) building off of that." Listen to "Airing Boston Celtics grievances, and feats of strength to fix them" on Spreaker. item.title: Liverpool receive huge injury boost ahead of Everton clash
item.description: Liverpool receive huge injury boost ahead of Everton clash Liverpool Injury Update: Victor Munoz Boost Ahead of Everton Clash Liverpool have one less problem than they feared ahead of the Merseyside derby. Victor Munoz, forced off in the 3-0 win over Club Brugge, has avoided serious injury. That matters, because Liverpool are already short of options and Andoni Iraola is still likely to be without Cody Gakpo and Ryan Gravenberch against Everton. Munoz went down after a heavy challenge at the end of a strong run in midweek. It looked awkward, enough to raise concerns about his knee, and enough for him to leave the pitch before half-time. The early signs, however, are positive. Iraola delivered the update in clear terms: “With Victor, I think the good news is that after assessing him, there is no disruption in the knee, everything is fine. But he has a big knock. It’s a big knock.” That does not guarantee availability for Sunday, but it changes the picture. A ligament issue would have meant weeks or months. A bruise means a late call. Iraola added: “He hasn’t trained today but he wants to try tomorrow. We’ll see how the bruise is. But I cannot tell you right now.” Liverpool would rather have Munoz than gamble unnecessarily, particularly in a derby where physical pressure is guaranteed from the first whistle. Photo: IMAGO Cody Gakpo absence remains clear There is less ambiguity with Gakpo. He will miss out, full stop. The forward has a calf problem picked up on international duty with the Netherlands and this will be his third consecutive missed match. Iraola was direct: “Cody definitely not [available against Everton]. It’s a muscle injury so we have to wait a little bit until the process goes on and it heals.” The timescale sounds ordinary enough, but muscle injuries rarely care for neat schedules. Iraola said: “This kind of injury is normally two or three weeks. He did it in the last [Netherlands] game against Germany, so normally it’s this timeline. But normally I don’t like to say timelines with injuries because every injury is different and some of them go quicker than others. It wasn’t a big injury but there is something there and you have to give the time to heal.” Ryan Gravenberch still struggling with heel pain Gravenberch is the more frustrating case. Heel pain sounds minor until it lingers for a month, which is exactly what has happened. He has not featured since the Carabao Cup last-16 win over Chelsea and there is still no clean return date. Iraola admitted: “It’s going to be difficult. I cannot say no because these kinds of injuries are difficult.” He explained the problem properly: “They don’t look like a big thing but you have the pain, it doesn’t go. Sometimes it’s better, you don’t know why. The next day, you come and it’s worse. He is dealing with this situation, we are trying to help him. The forward has a calf problem picked up on international duty with the Netherlands and this will be his third consecutive missed match. Iraola was direct: “Cody definitely not [available against Everton]. Iraola said: “This kind of injury is normally two or three weeks. He did it in the last [Netherlands] game against Germany, so normally it’s this timeline. Munoz has a chance, Gakpo is out, Gravenberch remains doubtful. For Iraola, the equation is simple enough. Get through the derby with enough attacking threat, avoid turning manageable injuries into longer absences, and take the good news where it comes.

item.title: What the Warriors are now privately saying about Draymond Green
item.description: Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images The Golden State Warriors face a tough decision when it comes to Draymond Green’s future. Draymond Green is putting up 3.6 points, 4.8 rebounds, and 6.3 assists in the 2026-27 regular season for Golden State. His passing still moves the rock, but his discipline and decision-making have hurt the team, including a flagrant foul against San Antonio and a recent back-and-forth with Eddie Johnson after Johnson questioned his value and Hall of Fame case. With offense already hard to come by for the Warriors, critics keep asking what else he adds on the floor. Golden State Warriors open to trading Draymond Green Sam Amick, who was speaking on Sactown , says the Warriors still appreciate everything Draymond Green has done for the franchise, though they’re open to moving him if the right trade comes up. He said: “I’ve said before yes, and it’s always like you feel like you’re breaking Warriors code if you say that, but yes. “Yeah, absolutely. Even after four rings together, other teams can bring him up without Golden State hanging up right away. He still has plenty of playoff savvy and defensive bite, but the Warriors are already short on points and he gives them next to nothing as a scorer. When buckets are that hard to come by, having a guy who doesn’t score on the floor makes things even tougher. item.title: Füllkrug scores late to rescue Bremen draw against Gladbach
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Werder Bremen's Niclas Füllkrug celebrates scoring his side's fourth goal during the German Bundesliga soccer match between Werder Bremen and Hamburger SV at the Weserstadion. (is associated with: «Füllkrug scores late to rescue Bremen draw against Gladbach») Carmen Jaspersen/dpa Niclas Füllkrug scored in stoppage time to rescue Werder Bremen a point in a 3-3 Bundesliga draw against last-placed Borussia Mönchengladbach on Friday. The hosts recovered from a 3-1 deficit in what was set to be a shocking defeat to Gladbach. Kevin Diks scored Gladbach's opener from the spot in the 27th minute after a handball by Youri Regeer. Eren Dinkci equalized for Bremen in the 38th, but the guests retook the lead right after the break as Honorat completed a composed finish in the 46th. The French midfielder added a second to his name in the 78th, completing a fulminant counterattack with a stunning curler from the edge of the box. It looked like Gladbach was taking all three points until Dinkci also got himself a brace in the 85th and league's top scorer Füllkrug took advantage of a defensive mistake to equalize in the second minute of stoppage time. Ahead of the weekend's matches, Bremen remain sixth, in the qualification spot for the Conference League, while Gladbach are bottom of the table with just one win in 11 matches. "Gladbach aren't exactly where they should be in the standings. When you watch the last few games, it's been tight. Today they did well, they caused us problems," Füllkrug told broadcaster Sky. "We were careless in the way we played. We have to play a clean football, we have to bring in quality." The weekend's schedule includes Hamburg v Bayern Munich on Saturday and leaders Borussia Dortmund v Bayer Leverkusen on Sunday.

item.description: DETROIT — Say this much for the Mid-American Conference. It's got this parity thing down pat, at least in football. Buffalo is in the MAC championship game in Pete Lembo's second season as head coach, while Toledo is in the championship game in Mike Jacobs' first season as head coach. Their wins eliminated defending champion Western Michigan (8-4, 6-2) from contention. Five teams entered Friday still in contention to play in the MAC championship game, including Ohio and Miami (Ohio). Western Michigan beat Miami in last year's championship game , 23-13. The last team to repeat as MAC champion was Northern Illinois, which won in 2011 and 2012. If Buffalo beats Toledo next Saturday, the MAC championship will see a seventh different winner in the last seven years. Buffalo last won a MAC championship in 2008, while Toledo last won in 2022. item.description: (Video): Emegha’s quick reactions and well-timed run give Chelsea a chance Emmanuel Emegha has given Chelsea their only positive moment from another defeat with a goal against Nottingham Forest. If you enjoy Talk Chelsea coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content. Chelsea have got a goal back against Nottingham Forest. Emmanuel Emegha came on at half time and has made a difference already. He was sniffing around for a ball to drop, and when Pedro Neto’s shot hit a defender the Dutchman had his chance. He stayed onside and reacted quickly to put the ball into the net. There was a long VAR check – but the summer signing had successfully stayed on the right side of the offside line. You can see Emegha’s strike in the clip embedded here: [Footage from Sky Sports] Alonso’s Emegha call is puzzling again Emmanuel Emegha. (Photo by Gareth Copley/Getty Images) The real question is why Emegha didn’t start the game. Most fans were expecting that – he scored a goal last week and his speed allows him to affect the game far more than the lumbering Welbeck, who is seemingly only useful when your team is dominating the game in the opposition’s box. Perhaps Emegha is not yet fit for 90 minutes. But in that case he should have started and come off later. It was one of a number of puzzling lineup decisions from the manager tonight. In other news… Wesley Fofana was taken off in the second half after picking up a yellow for two dreadful compounding errors. Chelsea’s stats from the first half against Forest were truly awful – although you only had to watch the game to know how bad it was. Xabi Alonso spoke about his team selection for tonight, and it’s pretty clear what he’s aiming for from what he’s said.

item.description: Brock Purdy update doesn't bode well for 49ers to have him for Seahawks game originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The San Francisco 49ers , coming off a dominant 35-10 victory over the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday Night Football in Week 11, are facing a big challenge in Week 12. Going up against their NFC West division rival Seattle Seahawks , the 49ers are not going to have an easy matchup on their hands. Colton McKivitz, their starting right tackle, is done for the year. Unfortunately, he might not be the only injury this team is dealing with. As Matt Barrows of The Athletic reports, quarterback Brock Purdy wasn't at practice Friday, which doesn't bode well for his odds of suiting up against the Seahawks. Brock Purdy's odds to play vs. Seahawks in Week 12 aren't looking good "No Brock Purdy sightings early on in Friday's practice," Barrows reports. "He did not practice Wednesday and Thursday." This is not the kind of report that the 49ers fanbase will like to hear. Purdy, their MVP candidate this season, is looking to be very questionable to play this week. Purdy is dealing with an ankle injury right now, and he was a non-participant at both Wednesday's and Thursday's practices. Seeing Purdy at practice on Friday would've calmed the fears of the 49ers about not having Purdy in Week 12 against a challenging Seahawks defense. While Mac Jones is capable of playing well in a backup role, as he did last year, there's a big difference between a competent backup like Jones and an MVP candidate like Purdy. MORE : Solving the Brian Flores puzzle: How Kyle Shanahan finally bested defensive guru in 49ers win After Purdy didn't show up at Friday's practice, at least at the beginning of practice, the odds of Purdy suiting up in Week 12 against the Seahawks aren't looking good. This season, Purdy has 2,624 passing yards and 23 touchdowns to just five interceptions. In his last game against the Seahawks, he went 19 of 29 for 189 yards, two touchdowns, and one interception in a win. At 10-1, the 49ers are in great shape to make the playoffs. Resting Purdy for a week would make sense, as the 49ers need to think about the playoffs now with their strong record. While winning the No. 1 seed and the NFC West are important things to consider, there's still a lot of season left. A loss to the Seahawks in Week 12 wouldn't be the end of the world. Besides, Jones could win this game, and it wouldn't be a huge surprise. Purdy hasn't shown up to practice this week for the 49ers, and his odds of playing in Week 12 aren't looking good. Based on this report from Barrows, 49ers fans might have to realize that Purdy might really miss this week as he deals with an ankle injury. item.title: LeBron James Triple-Double Lifts Sixers Past Heat On Wednesday
item.description: Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images LeBron James proved he can carry the Philadelphia 76ers even when their best player sits out. On Wednesday night, James recorded his first triple-double in a Sixers uniform, posting 25 points, 12 assists and 10 rebounds to lead the team to a 111-104 victory over the Miami Heat. The win moves the Sixers to a 15-4 record on the season and keeps their NBA Cup dreams alive, according to Sports Illustrated . This performance shows that Philadelphia does not need to rely solely on Joel Embiid to win games. The team faced a tough test with Embiid ruled out due to illness. James stepped up immediately, scoring 14 consecutive points in the second quarter. With 16 points, 6 rebounds, and 6 assists, he closed out the first half. In the opening half, he made all three of his long-range shots, showing hot form. This offensive flow allowed the Sixers to control the pace against a Miami team that had won seven games in a row. Maxey Delivers When It Counts Tyrese Maxey provided the extra scoring punch the team desperately needed. With Jaylen Brown sidelined for the second half due to a hamstring injury, Maxey took over. The game ended with him scoring a team-high 30 points, plus four rebounds and six assists. According to The Lufkin Daily News , this was Maxey’s third 30-point game of the season. He was efficient on offense, hitting 12 of his 21 field goal attempts. His ability to create his own shot was vital in a game where the Sixers were short-handed. James also hit 50 percent or better from the floor in four straight contests. He is finding his rhythm quickly with this new team. The combination of James and Maxey created a scoring threat that Miami could not stop. Even without Embiid, the Sixers found a way to win a close contest. The 111-104 final score reflects how tight the game was, but the result was clear. Heat Streak Snapped in Philadelphia The loss ended Miami’s seven-game winning streak. Giannis Antetokounmpo led the Heat with 32 points and 14 rebounds, but it was not enough. Davion Mitchell tallied 20 points alongside 10 assists, whereas Bam Adebayo notched 17 points and 11 rebounds. The Heat now sit at 2-1 in NBA Cup play, just like the Sixers. Both teams have one game remaining in their group. The Miami Heat face New York, the defending NBA Cup champion, in Friday night’s Group B final. The Sixers will look to build on this momentum as they continue their push for the title.

item.title: Raiders’ Jackson Powers-Johnson suffers potentially serious injury at practice
item.description: An already-frustrating season for Raiders offensive lineman Jackson Powers-Johnson took an ominous turn Friday when he suffered a potentially serious injury during practice. Powers-Johnson was ruled out for Sunday’s game against the Browns and could be sidelined considerably longer. “He had an injury at practice today, and we’ll have more details for you tomorrow,” Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Friday. Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza (15) celebrates a touchdown with Jackson Powers-Johnson (58) and Connor Heyward (34) in Las Vegas, Nov. 15, 2026. AP Photo/David Becker Asked if the injury was serious, Kubiak acknowledged the possibility. “Could be, yes,” Kubiak said. “We’ll go take a peek at him here after this and have more info for you.” It’s the latest setback for a player whose first three NFL seasons have fallen short of the lofty expectations that accompanied his arrival in Las Vegas. Jackson Powers-Johnson of the Las Vegas Raiders arrives at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, for a game against the Seattle Seahawks. Getty Images The Raiders selected Powers-Johnson with the 44th overall pick in the second round of the 2024 NFL Draft out of Oregon, where he won the Rimington Trophy as college football’s best center. The expectation was that Powers-Johnson would become a foundational piece along the Raiders’ offensive line, either at center or guard. Instead, injuries and an inability to establish himself as a permanent starter have prevented that from materializing. Powers-Johnson started 14 games as a rookie, splitting time between left guard and center. His second season was cut short by an ankle injury. Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak speaks during a news conference after an NFL football game in Denver, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. AP Photo/David Zalubowski The offseason signing of Tyler Linderbaum effectively closed the door on Powers-Johnson becoming the Raiders’ long-term answer at center. And he has been unable to maintain a firm grip on the starting right guard job. Now, depending on the severity of Friday’s injury, Powers-Johnson could face yet another obstacle in his effort to establish himself as part of the Raiders’ future, with next season representing the final year of his rookie contract.

Las Vegas Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza (15) celebrates a touchdown with Jackson Powers-Johnson (58) and Connor Heyward (34) in Las Vegas, Nov. 15, 2026. AP Photo/David Becker Asked if the injury was serious, Kubiak acknowledged the possibility. “Could be, yes,” Kubiak said. “We’ll go take a peek at him here after this and have more info for you.” It’s the latest setback for a player whose first three NFL seasons have fallen short of the lofty expectations that accompanied his arrival in Las Vegas. Jackson Powers-Johnson of the Las Vegas Raiders arrives at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, for a game against the Seattle Seahawks. Getty Images The Raiders selected Powers-Johnson with the 44th overall pick in the second round of the 2024 NFL Draft out of Oregon, where he won the Rimington Trophy as college football’s best center. The expectation was that Powers-Johnson would become a foundational piece along the Raiders’ offensive line, either at center or guard. Instead, injuries and an inability to establish himself as a permanent starter have prevented that from materializing. Powers-Johnson started 14 games as a rookie, splitting time between left guard and center. His second season was cut short by an ankle injury. Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak speaks during a news conference after an NFL football game in Denver, Sunday, Nov. 22, 2026. AP Photo/David Zalubowski The offseason signing of Tyler Linderbaum effectively closed the door on Powers-Johnson becoming the Raiders’ long-term answer at center. And he has been unable to maintain a firm grip on the starting right guard job. Now, depending on the severity of Friday’s injury, Powers-Johnson could face yet another obstacle in his effort to establish himself as part of the Raiders’ future, with next season representing the final year of his rookie contract.

item.title: Serie A | Venezia 0-0 Bologna: Stanković and Skorupski stand firm in stalemate
item.description: Serie A | Venezia 0-0 Bologna: Stanković and Skorupski stand firm in stalemate Filip Stanković and Łukasz Skorupski were the stars at the Penzo as bottom-of-the-table Venezia held Bologna to a goalless draw, with Redouane Halhal having an early opener ruled out by VAR. Venezia came into the game bottom of Serie A with six points from 12 games, after a 4-0 thrashing at Juventus on Sunday. Davide Nicola was without the injured Franjić, Šverko and Thierry Correia, but handed a start to Gianluca Busio in midfield. Bologna, ninth on 18 points, had drawn 1-1 with Udinese last week . Raffaele Palladino left Riccardo Orsolini and Artem Dovbyk on the bench, while Lorenzo De Silvestri, Emil Holm, Juan Miranda, Oussama El Azzouzi and Ukko Happonen were all injured. Venezia made the brighter start, and Skorupski had to dive low to his right to keep out John Yeboah’s effort after a defence-splitting pass from Akor Adams. The hosts thought they had taken the lead in the 14th minute. Halhal burst into the box to meet Antoine Hainaut’s whipped cross and finish into the bottom corner. However, the goal was ruled out for offside after a lengthy VAR check. Tempers flared in the aftermath, with Juan Jesus and Nadir Zortea both booked for dissent, and Martin Vitík and Hainaut soon joined them in the book. Skorupski was the busier goalkeeper in the first half. He produced a sharp save to deny Kike Pérez’s low volley on the half-hour, then thwarted Yeboah again from inside the box shortly before the break. At the other end, Jens Odgaard fired over from a good position and Arthur Theate headed straight at Stanković. Bologna improved after the restart, with Matteo Darmian on for Vitík. Stanković pulled off a superb reflex save to keep out Nicolò Casale’s header, and Federico Bernardeschi curled just wide from a set piece moments later. VENICE, ITALY – NOVEMBER 27: Riccardo Orsolini of Bologna FC during the Serie A match between Venezia FC and Bologna FC at Stadio Pier Luigi Penzo on November 27, 2026 in Venice, Italy. (Photo by Maurizio Lagana/Getty Images) Venezia 0-0 Bologna: Juan Jesus hits the post in dramatic second half Palladino turned to Orsolini and Nicolò Cambiaghi just before the hour, while Nicola sent on Thórir Jóhann Helgason for Busio. Helgason almost had an immediate impact. His set-piece delivery found Juan Jesus, whose header from the edge of the six-yard box came back off the post. Bologna brought on Roberto Piccoli for Odgaard, and he blazed over from Rahim Alhassane’s cross. Venezia refreshed their attack with Albion Rrahmani and Lion Lauberbach, and the latter forced a strong save from Skorupski at his near post. The chances kept coming in the closing stages. Stanković denied Lewis Ferguson’s header and then made his best save of the night to stop Tommaso Pobega from inside the six-yard box. Skorupski rushed out to smother Helgason’s effort at the other end, and Alhassane fired high and wide. Venezia 0-0 Bologna

Yet this proved the falsest of dawns, with Andoni Iraola’s nascent side perhaps caught in a bad moment. City have since managed one league victory ( 3-2 over Ipswich , six days later) and two more wins in regulation time (in the Champions League) in 10 matches. The sequence includes one point from the past four league fixtures. Maresca argues that his, too, is an embryonic project so there will be uneven form. “I am not a magician,” he said on Friday. But it is also fair to ponder whether, after the adrenaline surge of an us-against-the-world mentality carried City to the Liverpool and Ipswich wins, the grim reality of what the guilty verdict may mean for careers is affecting players. There is as much chance of Mike McCarthy settling down for Christmas dinner with Aaron Rodgers as there is of County missing out on promotion back to Scotland’s second tier. An assessment from the captain, Brian Graham, of a frankly irrelevant loss on penalties to Stenhousemuir in the Challenge Cup epitomises the County approach. “We should have been five- or six-nil up at half-time,” an irked Graham says. “That shows the standards we have set. item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Liam Delap can exploit Chelsea’s defensive woes while Senne Lammens is under pressure against Brentford Nottingham Forest’s last couple of seasons have been a story of good runs and bad runs, but it may help to know that last season’s encounters with Chelsea both presaged changes of fortune. After they lost to Chelsea in October, a seventh defeat in 10 winless games, Forest’s form improved and they won seven of their next 12 in all competitions. But after beating Chelsea in May, their seventh victory in a 10-game unbeaten run, Forest’s form dipped dramatically and they have won only twice since. Oliver Glasner’s criticism of players whose “standards [are] not high enough” is clearly designed to raise them. Time will tell if it has worked but the key man this week is one who should have no issues with motivation and whose English is at least decent. Liam Delap, facing the side that signed and swiftly discarded him, could really trouble Wesley Fofana and Levi Colwill. The Chelsea centre-back pairing were described as playing like “two novices” by Jamie Carragher after they were outfought by Dominic Calvert-Lewin last week. “Until they sign that dominant centre-back and leader, they’ve got absolutely no chance of achieving anything,” Carragher concluded. item.title: Thomas Frank earns first Crystal Palace win as McNeil cuts down Real Sociedad
item.description: Football seasons can pivot on certain moments and Thomas Frank will hope that Crystal Palace’s turning point came 17 minutes from full time here. Deservedly trailing to Mamadou Sarr’s goal having been second best throughout against Real Sociedad, this game – and perhaps the south London club’s entire trajectory – was turned on its head after Jon Martín was sent off for denying Jean-Philippe Mateta an equaliser. The France striker made no mistake with his penalty before Dwight McNeil – who made up for scoring an own goal in Saturday’s defeat by Coventry capped an extraordinary comeback in Frank’s first home match since succeeding Pierre Sage. Despite Yéremy Pino’s saved penalty in stoppage time and a number of other chances that were squandered, Dean Henderson pulled off a stunning late save to seal the victory and revive Palace’s Europa League campaign. Suddenly Palace have hope where there appeared to be none and the Premier League’s bottom side will head into Sunday’s crucial showdown with Hull with a spring in their step. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Bayern Munich go from bad to worse with own goals on and off the pitch
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Bayern Munich’s 2-1 defeat to Lille was arguably the most eye-catching of Wednesday night’s Bigger Cup results, but anyone who tuned into proceedings at Stade Pierre-Mauroy will have been unsurprised by the outcome. Not so much an elite European tie as a game of Name That Bayern Reserve, the German champions’ starting lineup resembled a pale facsimile of its usual self. Their current knack-list includes such high-profile names as – deep breath – Harry Kane, Michael Olise, Alphonso Davies, Manuel Neuer, Serge Gnabry, Luis Díaz, Jamal Musiala and Ismael Saibari. And with Díaz and Musiala only fit enough for places on the bench, Konrad Laimer was deployed as a makeshift striker. The veteran right-back is famously as handy as a small pot, but filling Kane’s iconic Skechers proved a task too far for the Austrian. I liked Erling Haaland’s observation that football can simultaneously be “easy and difficult” [yesterday’s Football Daily]. That got me thinking about other things that have conflicting characteristics. Soup can be both sweet and sour. My feelings for my partner often run hot and cold. And my daily tea-timely newsletter can be mildly funny and mildly unfunny – Mike Wilner. The constant change in Watford manager, a once fine club whose first two managers lasted a total of 23 years, is now so high that I don’t even notice it anymore ... apparently this was yesterday, and I’ve no idea who the previous bloke was. Watford are now onto their 30th manager, including caretakers, although in practice they’re all just caretaker managers, since the Pozzos took over in 2012. I don’t know whether to laugh at, or cry for, the Watford fans (Narrator: it’s the former, obviously) – Noble Francis. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.title: Alejandro Garnacho and the curious case of Aston Villa’s outcast loanees | Ben Fisher
item.description: Unai Emery wanted the winger but, like Harvey Elliott last season, he has been left out in the cold despite Villa’s attacking struggles It is three years this week since Alejandro Garnacho opened the scoring for Manchester United in a 3-3 draw at Galatasaray in the Champions League, on a typically boisterous night in Istanbul when Victor Lindelöf and Aaron Wan-Bissaka, now his teammates at Aston Villa, were also among the starters. At the time, Garnacho was a teenage star flourishing on the grandest of stages, a fixture in the United team and fresh from scoring an outrageous overhead kick at Goodison Park a few days earlier that would later clinch the Premier League’s goal-of-the-season award. He went on to score twice at Old Trafford on Boxing Day, in a 3-2 victory against Villa, and a couple of months later his double at home to West Ham was the catalyst for that iconic celebration photo of Garnacho, Kobbie Mainoo and Rasmus Højlund sitting on the advertising hoardings at the Stretford End, beaming smiles all round. All three were at the heart of United’s plans for a bright future, beacons of hope. At the end of that season, Garnacho signed off in style, he and Mainoo scoring against Manchester City at Wembley to win the FA Cup . Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League’s burst of early sendings-off may not last – but red cards are on the rise for a reason
item.description: While referees tend to reach for red early in the season before easing off, players are under increasing pressure to keep pace in a frenetic environment Off! Off! Off! The past three Premier League games have featured a red card, each for a different reason. Brighton’s Costinha was sent off for two bookings at Hull, Leny Yoro collected a red card against Liverpool for denying a goalscoring opportunity ( though his suspension was overturned on appeal) and James Tarkowski saw red for serious foul play at Brentford. This season is shaping up to be an outlier in the VAR era of officiating in English football. The latest red cards took the Premier League total to 22 in 2026-27. The rate of 0.2 per game equates to 76 across the whole season, which would equal the Premier League record set in 2005-06. Refereeing has evolved in the past decade, though. The average across the seven completed campaigns since VAR was introduced is 0.12 per game, with a high of 0.15 in 2023-24. Continue reading...

item.title: Search for next USMNT head coach needs to prioritize competence over fame
item.description: The job of Mauricio Pochettino’s successor is to fine-tune a team on the up. That requires a bureaucrat rather than a figurehead First, let’s get the Pep Exception out of the way. Or perhaps we’d better call it the Guardiola Caveat. Regardless, the point is the same. If US Soccer can get Pep Guardiola to manage the United States men’s national team, it should. Because when you have the chance to employ the most successful and influential coach of his generation, the thinker who stands upstream of essentially every major tactical current of the last two decades, you just have to do it. But let us assume that US Soccer can’t appoint Guardiola, because he is only a few months into his post-Manchester City sabbatical and still busying himself defending his body of work . item.description: A new book charts the complicated relationship between the two legends, starting on a sunny afternoon in Rio in 1979 Pelé and Diego Maradona first met in April 1979, four months before the Argentinian led his country’s under-20 side to victory at the World Youth Cup. Maradona told a journalist friend that his dream was to meet the Brazilian, and after a few weeks of aborted attempts to bring them together – mostly because Diego did not want to travel on a Monday, the one day he had free for his girlfriend Claudia – the meeting finally took place in Rio. Reporter Guillermo Blanco, who was writing about the meeting for Argentinian sports magazine El Gráfico, got the OK from Pelé’s people and was so intent on making it happen that he checked Maradona onto a flight one Sunday night without telling him. He collared the young man after Argentinos Juniors played Huracán and then raced to the airport and put him on a plane with his father, his agent and a photographer. Continue reading...

item.title: Madness erupts as Sevilla deny Betis in wild end to Spain’s ‘derby of derbies’
item.description: Rivals have been heading in opposite directions in recent years but latest clash showed some things never change “If we didn’t celebrate a goal, especially in this game, that would be madness,” Kike Salas said. Instead, this was madness, the kind of moment a derby is meant to have, even if it has nothing else. It was late, it was lucky, and there wasn’t even a winner but right there, right then, at 24 minutes past 8pm on Saturday evening in the Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán Stadium, it felt like there was. Frankly it was a bit rubbish, as bad a goal as you’ll see, but it was also the best, practically Pelé against the Nazis . Suddenly there were arms and legs everywhere, tears too. Cameras confirmed it. Zoom in and there they are: actual, real life tears. In the 91st minute of the 146th meeting between Sevilla Fútbol Club and Real Betis Balompié – “derby of derbies” according to Luis García, the Sevilla coach for whom it was the first – Salas’s shot from 18 yards went through Marc Bartra’s legs and Álvaro Valles’s hands. The ball dribbled into the Betis net so apologetically it barely touched the net at all and hadn’t got there before Sevilla’s vice-captain was gone. Raised in Morón de la Frontera, to the south of a city divided , Salas joined Sevilla at 11; now, having levelled the game at 1-1, he went tearing towards the terraces, absolutely losing it like they were. item.title: Mauricio Pochettino can now see just how desperate Manchester United are | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The manager’s first game in charge was a disaster and he needs to lift the mood within a sunken squad if a relegation battle is to be avoided Sign up for our free newsletter here In as much as any derby can ever be a free hit, there was always a sense that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Manchester United manager wouldn’t matter too much; nobody expected them to win away to Liverpool. This was not a game on which anybody was going to judge him, and that feeling only magnified when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes. United’s victory at Anfield last season was their first for a decade; what’s difficult to do with 11 men is only going to get harder playing a man down for 82 minutes. But that does not mean that it did not matter. Although Roy Keane was determined to reject the suggestion, there was perhaps even some credit to be gleaned from having lost only 4-0 . Certainly when they were 2-0 down after 13 minutes, there was reason for United to fear an embarrassment akin to their 7-0 defeat against Liverpool in 2023 . Perhaps Pochettino deserves credit for his switch to a back three, which brought a degree of stabilisation, but United could easily have lost far more comfortably than they did. Liverpool had 18 shots in the game three-and-a-half years ago, eight of them on target; on Sunday they had 28, 11 of them on target. item.content:encoded: The manager’s first game in charge was a disaster and he needs to lift the mood within a sunken squad if a relegation battle is to be avoided Sign up for our free newsletter here In as much as any derby can ever be a free hit, there was always a sense that Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Manchester United manager wouldn’t matter too much; nobody expected them to win away to Liverpool. This was not a game on which anybody was going to judge him, and that feeling only magnified when Leny Yoro was sent off after eight minutes. United’s victory at Anfield last season was their first for a decade; what’s difficult to do with 11 men is only going to get harder playing a man down for 82 minutes. But that does not mean that it did not matter. Although Roy Keane was determined to reject the suggestion, there was perhaps even some credit to be gleaned from having lost only 4-0 . Certainly when they were 2-0 down after 13 minutes, there was reason for United to fear an embarrassment akin to their 7-0 defeat against Liverpool in 2023 . Perhaps Pochettino deserves credit for his switch to a back three, which brought a degree of stabilisation, but United could easily have lost far more comfortably than they did. Liverpool had 18 shots in the game three-and-a-half years ago, eight of them on target; on Sunday they had 28, 11 of them on target. When you’ve conceded an xG of 4.38, there’s not much point quibbling over the details; you’ve been hammered. Continue reading...

item.title: Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden
item.description: The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quickly It’s injury time at the Emirates on 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Tottenham. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. item.description: Spain Under-21 striker admits the pace of the Premier League has surprised him but says he must stay calm over goal drought at Fulham The first thing Rita Hayworth’s great nephew says when he walks in is: “Sorry I’m late.” Gonzalo García is not late, but it’s very like him: he is impeccably polite, accommodating, and there’s an almost gentle quality to him, a calm that’s not common but can help, especially in moments when the pressure builds. There’s a reason one of the coaches standing in the rain by the pitch where Spain’s under‑21s have just finished training says everyone here loves García. The Fulham striker shakes hands, introduces himself and ducks into the dressing room to change; then a few minutes later he’s back, apologising for a wait that wasn’t one. Time to talk, so let’s start with Tinseltown, the family tale. García laughs. His great-aunt, born Margarita Carmen Cansino, was among the biggest stars in Hollywood, although he’s not sure he’s seen any of her films. His grandfather was a surgeon and others in the family followed. His uncles played rugby for Spain, but that wasn’t his thing. As for him, he enrolled in a degree in business management and analytics, and reckons he might have liked law, yet even that wasn’t his chosen field. Continue reading...

item.title: WSL talking points: Chelsea’s gamble pays off and have Arsenal lost fear factor?
item.description: Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL draw Sonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. Bompastor said after the game that she had not spoken to Buchanan but that she would “explain myself to her”. “I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I’m always direct and honest so they have the information,” she said. “It won’t be any different.” Enforced or not, the substitution was a huge gamble that paid off, even after the loss of Melvine Malard to injury in the first half reduced their number of remaining in-game substitution windows to one. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. And we’ll set you up for the weekend and let you know our live coverage plans so you’ll be ahead of the game. Here’s what you can expect from us. Try our other sports emails: there’s daily football news and gossip in The Fiver , and weekly catch-ups for cricket in The Spin and rugby union in The Breakdown . Living in Australia?
